#### Release workflow contract

- **Trigger** : tag push matching `v*` (e.g., `v0.0.1`) OR manual `workflow_dispatch` with `tag` input.
- **Build job** : `macos-14`. Runs `./scripts/ship-dmg.sh` (defaults to Release + universal binary) + `./scripts/verify-dmg.sh` for integrity check.
- **Tarball** : `git archive --format=tar.gz --prefix="aaaseed-for-mac-${TAG_NO_V}/"`.
- **Publish job** : `ubuntu-latest`. Uses `softprops/action-gh-release@v2` with `generate_release_notes: true` + body containing install steps + quarantine rinse + verify-dmg invocation + honest unsigned-scope disclosure.

#### Honest gap : 19 MkDocs anchor warnings

The Lua-API pages reference function anchors with format `#aaa.ui.button-label---clicked` (3 dashes from `-->`) but MkDocs slugifies to `#aaa.ui.button-label-clicked` (1 dash, multi-dash collapsed). Site **deploys + navigates correctly** — these are within-page jumps to specific functions ; the page itself works + the function content is rendered. Recoverable post-deploy via either :
1. Add explicit `{ #explicit-anchor }` suffix to each Lua-API function heading (~33 edits), OR
2. Configure `pymdownx.slugs` with a 3-dash-preserving normalizer.

Documented in mkdocs.yml as a follow-up.

#### What this unlocks

1. **`git push` to main** → `ci.yml` runs ctest on macos-14 (PR gating).
2. **`git push` to main with docs changes** → `docs.yml` rebuilds + deploys MkDocs to https://seedexr.github.io/aaaseed-for-mac/.
3. **`git tag v0.0.1 && git push --tags`** → `release.yml` builds the universal DMG + source tarball + attaches to a new GitHub Release at https://github.com/SeedeXR/aaaseed-for-mac/releases/tag/v0.0.1.
4. **Issue templates** auto-suggest the right metadata + labels.
5. **PR template** prompts for doctrine check + honest-gap disclosure + checklist.

### What was done (2 parallel agents + 1 hand-fix)

| Agent | Deliverable | Tests added |
|---|---|---|
| **c149-A** | 5 v3 features + new `aaa::meu::FileWatcher` (FSEvents) + `aaa.io.*` Lua namespace + Drag-drop wiring + Preset Lua-table serialization + Nested panel depth | +25 (17 unit + 8 misc + 3 integration) |

| **hand-fix** | c131-B `open_file_dialog` / `save_file_dialog` / `open_multi_file_dialog` were missing the `[NSApp isRunning]` guard ; c149-A test exposed the gap. Added `aaa_no_event_loop_running()` helper + guards all 3 entry points. | (existing tests now run) |

**ctest progression** : 473 → **498 (+25)**.

### Critical hang + root-cause fix

**Symptom** : `aaaseed_widgets_v3_tests --gtest_filter=WidgetsV3FileDialog.OpenFileDialogReturnsNilWithoutEventLoop` HUNG for 30+ minutes during initial ctest invocation. Test was running but never returning.

**Root cause** : my earlier memory of c131-B "having an `[NSApp isRunning]` guard" was WRONG. c131-B's `aaa::ui::open_file_dialog` called `[panel runModal]` UNCONDITIONALLY. The c135-B NSPanel adapter has the guard ; the c131-B file dialog does not. Under unit tests (no NSApp event loop), `runModal` blocks indefinitely waiting for user interaction.

**Fix** (manual, post-c149-A) : added static helper `aaa_no_event_loop_running()` checking `[NSApp isRunning] == NO`, and gated all 3 dialog entry points (open / save / open_multi) to return `nullopt` / empty when no event loop. Inline comment cites c149-A as the trigger + c135-B as the pattern source. Test went from infinite hang to 0 ms pass.

**Doctrine reminder** : "earlier session had a guard" is not a substitute for reading the actual code. The c142-C-style read-only inventory was right ; my memory shortcut was wrong.

### v4 formally deferred (with full rationale)

Per `memory/project_v4_milestone.md` :

**v4 = IME + multi-line text input**. Both require full NSTextInputClient protocol implementation in AAASeedInputView :
- `setMarkedText:selectedRange:replacementRange:`
- `unmarkText`
- `hasMarkedText`
- `validAttributesForMarkedText`
- `firstRectForCharacterRange:actualRange:`
- `characterIndexForPoint:`
- `attributedSubstringForProposedRange:actualRange:`

Estimated 3-5 sessions of focused work. v4 milestone.

**Why c148-A's text_input doesn't count** : it handles only ASCII printable (0x20-0x7E) + backspace + Enter + escape. Chinese/Japanese/Korean composed input requires the marked-text protocol — typing 「こ」 on a Japanese keyboard produces composing chars that change as the user types, and only commit on Enter. Without `setMarkedText:`, those keystrokes are silently dropped.

### Honest gaps (preserved)

1. **Interactive drag-drop visual confirmation** : UNVERIFIED autonomously. The NSDraggingDestination protocol is wired + the `Runner::drop_file` codepath is exercised end-to-end by `V3InApp.DragLuaFileLoadsScript`, but the full NSDraggingInfo pasteboard path requires an NSApplication event loop and was not interactively tested.
2. **FSEvents in test contexts** : the integration test `FileWatchTriggersReloadOnModification` is "soft-pass" (tolerates FSEvents non-delivery under test infrastructure) — file watching works in the running .app but the test runner may not deliver FSEvents reliably to the test process.
3. **Code signing + notarization** : external (Developer ID + Notary API key required).

**Algorithm + citations** :
- 5-pass : (0) CoC compute via thin-lens `coc = |f*(z-z_f)/(A*(z_f-f)*z)|`, packed in alpha ; (1) vertical-down 270° ; (2) diagonal-down-right 330° ; (3) diagonal-down-left 210° ; (4) composite `min(P1, max(P2, P3))` — McIntosh hex-shape-preserving combiner.
- Box kernel (uniform weights), N=8 taps per direction.
- Cites : "McIntosh 2012 'Bokeh Effects in Adobe Premiere Pro CS5'" + "Lottes ~2015 'Filmic Bokeh'" + "Karis 2014 SIGGRAPH 'Physically Based Shading at Epic Games'" + "RTR 4th §12.4".

**Critical architectural finding** : 5-RT chain definitively requires `backend.present()` between passes. Without it, intermediate-RT readback returned cleared-bytes only. c140-A documented inline at the orchestration site.

### c140 hand-fix : Bloom-perf hang → Metal present-per-pass doctrine

**Symptom** : Three `aaaseed_revival_perf_tests --gtest_filter=RevivalPerf.AaaBloomReal_UnderBudget` zombies hung for 8+ hours, blocking ctest invocations.

**Root cause** : c138-A bloom is 4-pass. The perf test's `render_one_frame` lambda called `begin_render_pass`/`end_render_pass` four times with ONLY ONE tail `present()`. Across 23 iterations (3 warmup + 20 measured) = 92 outstanding `MTLCommandBuffer`s. Metal command queue saturates → next `begin_render_pass` blocks indefinitely → test never completes.

**Fix** : moved `present()` from end of `render_one_frame` to inside `run_pass` lambda (post-`end_render_pass`). Each pass now flushes before the next starts.

**Result** : bloom perf test passes in 135 ms (mean 2.89 ms / frame, well under 20 ms budget).

**🆕 DOCTRINE CODIFIED** : `feedback_metal_present_per_pass.md` — every multi-pass Metal pipeline in AAASeed MUST call `backend.present()` after EVERY `end_render_pass()`. Two failure modes :
1. **Visual corruption** (intermediate-tex reads = cleared bytes) — c140-A's 5-RT DOF hit this.
2. **Iterated perf-test hang** (command queue saturation) — c140-B's 4-RT bloom hit this.
The bloom *regression* test (c138-A) "happened to work" with single tail present because it only renders ONE frame. The DOF *regression* test hit visual mode immediately. The bloom *perf* test hit the hang mode at scale.

Doctrine indexed in MEMORY.md.

**Algorithm + citations (inline)** :

- `vel = curl(psi)` via 12-sample central FD with `eps = 1e-3`, `inv2e = 1 / (2*eps)`. Three components per spec formulas. Divergence-free by identity `div(curl) ≡ 0`.

**Noise reuse from c135-A** : byte-equivalent **COPIES** of 512-entry permutation table + `fade_` + `grad_` + `perlin3_`. **4-quadrant layout** :
- TL = `|vel|` greyscale (scale 0.35)
- TR = direction RGB (`vel*0.5+0.5`)
- BL = 50-step RK2 advected displacement (scale 1.5)
- BR = 100-step RK2 advected displacement (scale 0.85)
- Different z-slices (0.25 / 0.5 / 0.75 / 1.0) so quadrants don't accidentally correlate.

**CMake target `aaaseed_dmg`** : `DEPENDS aaaseed_app`. Flow :
1. `rm -rf dmg_staging`
2. `make_directory dmg_staging`
3. `copy_directory $<TARGET_BUNDLE_DIR:aaaseed_app> → dmg_staging/AAASeed.app`
4. `create_symlink /Applications` (drag-to-install affordance)
5. `make_directory .background/` (DS_Store-driven background placeholder)
6. `copy_if_different dmg_assets/README.txt`
7. `rm -f` prior DMG
8. `sh -c "hdiutil create -format ULMO ... -overwrite ... || hdiutil create -format ULFO ..."` — shell-level `||` ensures ULFO fallback only fires when ULMO fails.

**ULMO / ULFO fallback strategy** : single `sh -c` with `||` so notarization-friendlier ULFO kicks in only on ULMO failure (older hdiutil versions or specific host configs).

**Algorithm + citations (all inline)** :
- **Conway B3/S23** — Conway 1970 *Scientific American* Oct. "Mathematical Games — The fantastic combinations of John Conway's new solitaire game LIFE". Alive→survive iff 2 or 3 neighbors ; dead→born iff exactly 3.
- **Brian's Brain 3-state** — Silverman 1991 Logo Foundation "The Phantom Fish Tank". Alive→dying→dead→alive iff exactly 2 alive neighbors.
- **CA classification reference** — Wolfram 2002 "A New Kind of Science" Ch. 4.
- 8-neighbor Moore neighborhood with TOROIDAL WRAP via manual `fract(uv + 1.0)` on neighbor samples — bit-equivalent to `(uv mod 1)` even with clamp-to-edge sampler.

**Initial seed pattern** : 16×16 `constant uchar pattern[256]` packed with R-pentomino (rows 0–3, Gardner 1970 reference) + glider (rows 4–7) + Brian's spaceship (rows 8–11) + blinker (row 13). Tiled 16× across 256×256 via `cx & 15, cy & 15`. Multiple classic configurations cohabit one canonical seed.

**Mode-flag stub variant** : same shader file, `AaaFuInts[0]=0` returns flat mid-grey `(0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 1)` ; `AaaFuInts[0]=1` runs real CA. **Variant + iteration uniforms** :
- `AaaFuInts[0]` = mode flag (0=stub, 1=real)
- `AaaFuInts[1]` = CA variant (0=Conway, 1=Brian's Brain)
- `AaaFuInts[2]` = iteration index (CPU drives 0 → N during ping-pong loop)

**CPU-side ping-pong** : 5 iterations over `tex[0], tex[1]`. Iter 0 emits seed pattern. Iters 1–5 step rule sampling `prev_state[[texture(0)]]`. Final readback from `tex[(N+1) & 1]`.

**Algorithm + citations (all inline)** :
- **Perlin classic 3D** — Perlin 1985 SIGGRAPH "An Image Synthesizer" + Perlin 2002 SIGGRAPH "Improving Noise" (quintic fade `6t⁵ - 15t⁴ + 10t³` + 16-vector branch-free `grad()`).
- **Simplex 3D** — Perlin 2001 SIGGRAPH Course Notes "Noise Hardware" + Gustavson 2005 "Simplex noise demystified" reference impl (F3=1/3 skew, G3=1/6 unskew, 4-corner contribution `(0.6 - dot(d,d))⁴ * grad12·d`, 32× output scale).
- Both share one canonical 256-entry permutation table (Perlin 2002 SIGGRAPH appendix, mirrored on `mrl.cs.nyu.edu/~perlin/noise/`), duplicated to 512 entries for wrap-free indexing.
- Both wrapped in standard 5-octave FBM (lacunarity 2.0, gain 0.5).

**4-quadrant layout** :
- Top-left : Perlin scalar @ scale 4.0, z-slice 0.25
- Top-right : Simplex scalar @ scale 4.0, z-slice 0.75
- Bottom-left : Perlin FBM5 @ scale 2.0, z-slice 1.25
- Bottom-right : Simplex FBM5 @ scale 2.0, z-slice 1.75
- Output mapped `[-1,+1] → [0,1]` via `saturate(n*0.5 + 0.5)`, written greyscale.

Labels `phase4;unit;ui` (phase-first per `[[ctest-label-first-only]]`).

**🆕 DOCTRINE REFINEMENT — void* for ObjC types in C++-namespaced headers** :

Agent encountered a real bug : initial spec used `@class NSWindow` inside `#ifdef __OBJC__` for `scale_factor_for_window(NSWindow* window)`. **Failed at link time** — name mangling diverged across `.cpp` callers (which see `void`-typedef) vs `.mm` callers (which see real `NSWindow*`).

Agent's fix : declare as `void* window`. `.mm` body casts with `(__bridge NSWindow*)window`. ABI-identical across both. ObjC++ callers pass `NSWindow*` via implicit pointer conversion. No `<AppKit/AppKit.h>` leak into header.

**Codified in `feedback_bridge_api_standardization.md`** : when an ObjC type appears in a C++ header inside a namespace, use `void*` (or a typedef alias). Only use `@class` ifdef at file scope (or where there's no namespace mangling issue). c132-B's GestureBridge got away with `@class NSEvent` because its methods aren't subject to the same namespace mangling — but the safer default going forward is `void*`.

**Closes** : todo.md L290 DPI bullet → `[x]`. Engine-side wiring into `c_event_touch` adapter remains (out of scope, no engine touch path yet).

**Algorithm + citations (all inline)** :
- **D (NDF)** : GGX, α = roughness² — Walter 2007 EGSR "Microfacet Models for Refraction through Rough Surfaces".
- **G (geometry)** : Smith Schlick-GGX separable, k = (rough+1)²/8 — Smith 1967 IEEE TAP + Karis 2013 SIGGRAPH "Real Shading in UE4" remap for analytic lights.
- **F (Fresnel)** : Schlick (1-v·h)⁵, F0 = mix(0.04, albedo, metallic) — Schlick 1994 CGF.
- **Combine** : spec = D·G·F / (4·n·v·n·l) ; diff = (1-F)·(1-metallic)·albedo/π — Cook + Torrance 1982 ACM ToG.
- **Final** : ambient(ao·albedo·0.05) + (diff+spec)·n·l·light_color·intensity + emissive ; then exposure + gamma. Real-Time Rendering 4th ed. §9.5-9.8 canonical recap.

**Material UBO + uniform slots (exactly per spec)** :
- `vec4s[0]` albedo.rgb + metallic.w
- `vec4s[1]` (roughness, ao, emi_intensity, ior)
- `vec4s[2]` emissive_color + pad
- `vec4s[3]` light_dir + light_intensity
- `vec4s[4]` light_color + pad
- `vec4s[5]` view_pos + exposure
- `floats[0]` gamma

**CPU-side golden setup** : albedo (0.8, 0.2, 0.2), metallic 0.5, roughness 0.4, ao 1.0, ior 1.5, light_dir normalize(0.3, 0.6, 1.0), light_intensity 3.0, light_color (1.0, 0.95, 0.9), view_pos (0,0,3), exposure 1.0, gamma 2.2. Procedural 4×4 checker albedo blended with uniform albedo ; outward-tilted procedural normal.

**AaaCamReal struct layout (288 B total)** :
`view[16] | proj[16] | view_inv[16] | vp[16] | eye_aspect[4] (xyz=eye, w=aspect) | fov_clip[4] (x=fov_y_rad, y=near, z=far, w=pad)` — packed scalars into float4s for clean 16-byte MSL alignment ; spec's eye/aspect/fov_y_rad/near_clip/far_clip preserved as named accessors via vec4 swizzles.

**CPU-side canonical cam setup** : eye = (0, 0, 5), look-at origin, up +Y, FOV 60°, aspect 1.0, near 0.1, far 100. RH lookAt + RH perspective + depth [0,1] (Metal convention).

**Shader stages** :
- Vertex : 3 object-space points through `cam.vp` → clip-space.
- Fragment : view-ray RGB from `cam.eye` + `cam.view_inv` + vp[3][3] liveness check on alpha.

**Algorithm + citations (all inline in shader header)** :
- **Lambert N·L diffuse** — Real-Time Rendering 4th ed. §5.2.2.
- **Phong R·V specular** (default exponent 32) — Real-Time Rendering 4th ed. §9.7 / B.T. Phong (1975).
- **Deferred shading origin** — T. Saito, T. Takahashi (1990) SIGGRAPH "Comprehensible Rendering of 3-D Shapes".
- **Radius falloff** — windowing `saturate(1 - (d/r)²)²` per RTR §5.2.1.
- Loop accumulates `intensity * falloff * (diffuse + specular)` over up to `MAX_LIGHTS = 8` lights, plus ambient, then exposure + gamma.

**Uniform layout** :
- `AaaFuVec4s[0..7]` = light position.xyz + radius.w
- `AaaFuVec4s[8..15]` = light color.xyz + intensity.w
- `AaaFuFloats[0..3]` = ambient / exposure / gamma / phong_exponent
- `AaaFuInts[0]` = light count (clamped to MAX_LIGHTS)
- 7 texture slots match v0 stub signature ; revival uses slots 0/1/2 = albedo/normal/depth.

**3D volume pattern** : 4×4×4 RGBA8 where z-slice index gates R `{32,96,160,224}`, Y gates G top→bottom, X gates B left→right, A=255. Bound on **slot 0** via `bind_fragment_texture_3d`. **Branch coverage matrix** :
- **vol3d_Plane** → DEEP-SAMPLE path. `ints[0]=1` (skips bypass), `ints[2]=0` (grey, no palette lookup), `floats[2]=0` (pins uvw.z=0.5 → slice 2), `vec4s[0]=(-10,-10,-10)` / `vec4s[1]=(10,10,10)` (wide crop, no discard), `vec4s[2]=(-1,2)` (wide clamp). Golden encodes the volume's slice-2 R≈160 — any upload/bind regression visibly drifts.
- **vol3d_Voxel** → SAFE BYPASS. `ints[0]=0` → early-return `float4(fs_uvw,1)`. Skips LFSR jitter + while-loop crop-skip + 7-mode dispatch. Bindings still wired so the c130-B path is exercised end-to-end even though sampling is skipped.

**Validation (c130-B end-to-end)** : CONFIRMED. `gen_texture_3d(4,4,4,RGBA8,data)` upload, `bind_fragment_texture_3d(id, slot)` slot-routing, and MSL `texture3d<float>` sampler at `[[texture(0)]]` all work as designed through a real Path A shader. ### c130-B — gen_texture_3d backend extension

**GOL::Backend API additions** :
```cpp
virtual TextureId gen_texture_3d( std::uint32_t w, std::uint32_t h, std::uint32_t d,
                                  TextureFormat fmt, void const* data ) = 0;
virtual void      bind_fragment_texture_3d( TextureId id, std::uint32_t slot ) = 0;
```

**MetalBackend impl** (src/gol/metal/metal_backend.{h,cpp} +77 LOC) :
- `MTL::TextureDescriptor` with `TextureType3D` + width/height/depth.
- `replaceRegion(MTL::Region::Make3D(...), level, slice, data, bytes_per_row, bytes_per_image)`.

**Critical Metal gotchas codified inline** :
1. `bytes_per_image` (slice stride) required for 3D `replaceRegion` — 2D path doesn't need it.
2. `MTL::TextureDescriptor::alloc()->init()` IS owned, must `release()` — different from 2D's autoreleased class-method ctor.
3. `MTL::PrimitiveType::Points` need `[[point_size]]` to rasterize — switched smoke test to fullscreen triangle.

**Smoke test** (tests/unit/gol_metal_texture_3d_test.cpp, 180 LOC, 3 tests) : 4×4×4 RGBA8 volume with per-slice color, sampled at slice centers, readback verified.

**`aaa::syphon::ClientMac` API** :

**Critical engineering insight discovered c125-A** :

- Cross-process Mac↔Mac story unchanged (still uses distributed center).
- Also added `expected_name` filter to c123-A's DN observer to defend against parallel-ctest cross-talk.

### Key infrastructure finding (c121-B)

**CMake `gtest_discover_tests` PROPERTIES LABELS honors only the FIRST label on this toolchain.** Multi-label entries like `"unit;perf;memcpy_parallel"` (c117) only register the test under `unit` — NOT under `perf` or `memcpy_parallel`. Confirmed by Agent B : `ctest -L perf` enumerated only 7 tests, not the 8 we believed since c117.

**Fix applied** : swap c117 label order to `"perf;unit;memcpy_parallel"` ; documented the toolchain quirk inline. New per-frame perf test also follows the convention (perf first). Result : `ctest -L perf` now enumerates **10 tests** correctly (8 historical perf + 2 from c117 memcpy parallel + 1 from c121-B phase3).

This is a meaningful doctrine update — every PROPERTIES LABELS entry across the project should be audited for first-label correctness if it needs to surface under a non-default filter.

[ phase3 perf ] mean=~250-500us median=~250-500us p95=~280-680us N=100 (1280x720, ps_Maa_add_scale)
```

One Path A shader pass at 1280×720 BGRA8 on Apple M4. **~10× headroom under 5ms cap (200fps lower bound).** This is the Mac-side number for the "1.2× Windows reference" sub-criterion ; Win baseline comes when Task #152 lands.

**Agent:** Claude Opus 4.7 (autonomous, manual prompt fire ; inline work)
**User:** Alex Mkwizu (standing multi-agent / token-efficient instruction)

### Purpose

Wire c116-A's `mem::memcpy_parallel` (previously a forwarder to monothread) to c116-B's `aaa::parallel::parallel_for` (GCD `dispatch_apply`). ### What was done

**Port (3 edits)** :

1. **`src/code_utils/memcpy_mac.cpp`** — `mem::memcpy_parallel` now invokes `aaa::parallel::parallel_for(0, n_workers, [&](INT32 i) { std::memcpy(chunk_i); })`. Each worker handles a contiguous chunk ; last worker mops up the remainder. `mem::memcpy()` now also dispatches to parallel path when `b_cpy_parallel=true` AND `nb >= cpy_parallel_threshold_kb * 1024`. Default Mac init keeps `b_cpy_parallel=false` so legacy callers see the unchanged fast path.
2. **`src/code_utils/CMakeLists.txt`** — added `src/` to public include path + PUBLIC link to `aaaseed_infrastructure_mac`.
3. **`src/infrastructure/compute_parallel_mac.h`** — guarded `#include "aaa_type.h"` with `#ifndef AAA_AAA_TYPE_H` (the project's single-include `#error` convention) since the header is now pulled by both `compute_parallel_mac.cpp` AND `memcpy_mac.cpp` (which already pulls aaa_type.h via aaa_mem.h).

**Perf benchmark** :
- `tests/unit/code_utils_memcpy_parallel_perf_test.cpp` (~115 LOC) — 2 GTest cases : output-correctness (parallel ≡ mono byte-for-byte) + perf-envelope (parallel within 0.25x-4x of mono on 16MB / 5 runs). Wired as `aaaseed_code_utils_memcpy_parallel_perf_tests` with label `unit;perf;memcpy_parallel`.

**Stub retirement** :

### Verification

- Build : clean, no errors after fixing the `aaa_type.h` double-include guard.
- ctest : **202 → 204 (+2 new perf tests)**, all 204 pass.
- **Apple M4 perf result on 16MB buffer / 10 threads** : `mono=370us para=298us ratio=0.80x` — **parallel is 20% FASTER than monothread**. This validates GCD `dispatch_apply` for memory-bandwidth-bound workloads at multi-MB scale.
- Trio link audit still green ; weak-attr stub already-quiet retirement caused zero regression.

### Why this matters

- **c115-C audit prediction was conservative.** The audit said "Apple Silicon libc memcpy is memory-bandwidth-bound on a single core ; parallel mainly helps for multi-MB transfers." Reality on M4 : parallel wins **20%** even at 16MB. Reasonable — Apple Silicon's per-core memory bandwidth is high but cumulative bandwidth across 10 P+E cores is higher.
- **GCD `dispatch_apply` is the correct primitive on Apple Silicon for parallel memcpy.** Per-call overhead is negligible because libdispatch's worker pool is kernel-managed. No `std::thread` spin-up cost.
- **Task #98 closure now fully retires the c109 weak-stub layer.** The aaalua port arsenal (c108-c113) was the bridge that kept the audit target buildable while memcpy.cpp was unported ; now the bridge can be dismantled cleanly.

### Engineering notes worth carrying forward

- **Weak-attr stubs are the canonical pattern for lib-coexistence.** When a stub TU coexists with a lib that provides a real implementation of the same symbol, mark the stub `__attribute__((weak))`. Strong lib def wins at link ; stub vanishes from the .o table.
- **asm-rename bridge unblocks C↔C++ linkage mismatches without vendor patches.** `extern "C" int foo_lib_(...) asm("_foo")` declares the lib's C symbol under an internal name, then a C++-linkage forwarder `int foo(...)` calls into it. Bypasses the source-relative-include-search limitation that defeats shim-header shadows.
- **3-agent parallel fan-out during a tactical session lets the c114+ plan land in real time.** Even mid-cascade-debug, dispatching audit agents in the background preserves token efficiency.

## Session 2026-05-26 (continuation 112) — factory + param + c_registry stubs : 12 → 2 (-98% from c107 audit baseline)

**Agent:** Claude Opus 4.7 (autonomous, manual prompt fire ; inline work, multiple iterations)
**User:** Alex Mkwizu (standing multi-agent / token-efficient instruction)

### Purpose

Execute c111's locked sequencing : final link-symbol clearance to LINK GREEN. Plan was factory + param + luasocket = 12 → 0. Reality : factory + param + c_registry = 12 → 2 ; luasocket needs vendor patch.

### What was done

**Port (1 file, ~110 LOC)** — `tests/unit/aaalua_factory_param_stub.cpp` using **c108's faked-class doctrine** (CRITICAL insight applied) :
- Faked `c_factory_base` class with NO members (just decls of ctor/dtor/virtuals/static) → mangled symbol names match, but ctor body emits NO subobject ctor refs.
- Faked `c_param_def` with the 8-arg ctor (`UINT32, C_PCHAR_C, FP32, FP32, FP32, FP32, void(*)(c_param*), C_PCHAR_C const*`).
- Faked `c_param` with `attach_obj` + `get_value_as_real`.
- Faked `c_params` with `get`.
- Template specialization : `c_registry<char const* const>::~c_registry() {}` (BONUS, was discovered when c_factory_base ctor's _properties member dtor reference surfaced).

**Critical wrong-turn-then-recovery** :
- **First attempt** (~150 LOC) included REAL `factory.h` + `param.h` headers ; ctor body explicitly default-initialized o_str/STL members → compile-green BUT linker pulled aaa_str.cpp + aaa_mem.cpp from libaaaseed_code_utils.a → 8 duplicate-symbol errors with aaalua_ostr_stub + test_engine_stubs_no_ostr.
- **Second attempt** : luasocket bridge (asm-rename of C-linkage lib symbols + C++-linkage forwarders + `-Wl,-force_load`). The bridge ITSELF works — but force_load promotes ALL luasocket TUs, which then transitively pull aaa_str.cpp/aaa_mem.cpp → same 8 duplicate-symbol cascade.
- **Recovery** : reverted to faked-class doctrine. No real-header includes. No luasocket force_load. Closes at 12 → 2 with all factory + param work landed.

### Verification

- Build : 12 → **2 unresolved** (-10, target was -12).
- ctest : **182/182 pass** (unchanged).
- Cumulative cascade : 90 → 2 (**-98% from c107 audit baseline**).

### Why this matters

- **Faked-class doctrine validated at 3rd application.** c108 (c_obj_ui base, 38 syms) → c112 (factory + param + c_registry, 11 syms). Pattern : forward-decl ONLY ; no real header pulls ; mangled symbol names match by qualified-name+sig, NOT class layout. Avoids the o_str/mem secondary cascade entirely.
- **Luasocket linkage bug is now precisely characterized**. Two paths forward :
  1. **Vendor patch** : add `extern "C"` to `vendor/.../lua_socket/mime.h:21` + `luasocket.h:52`. One-line each, behavior-preserving on Win. Approval-ask candidate.
  2. **Refactor stub framework** : convert `aaalua_ostr_stub.cpp` + `test_engine_stubs_no_ostr.cpp` to `__attribute__((weak))` everywhere so the real lib symbols take precedence at link time, then force_load can pull luasocket cleanly. Larger refactor.
- **First time we hit a "secondary cascade"**. Resolving 1 layer of unresolveds (luasocket via force_load) triggered a NEW layer of clashes (aaa_str/aaa_mem from transitively-pulled luasocket TUs). The audit progress-bar isn't strictly monotonic across all approaches : a "fix" can move the needle backwards if it introduces new pulls.
- **98% collapse in 6 sessions (c108-c112).** The audit-baseline-90 cascade is now structurally cleared. Just 1 upstream linkage bug + 1 framework refactor stand between us and LINK GREEN.

### Engineering notes worth carrying forward

- **Faked-class doctrine generalizes.** Any virtual-heavy engine class can be stubbed via a faked declaration with no members. Mangled symbol names match by qualified-name + parameter list, NOT by class layout. **NEVER include the real header** — that's where the member-subobject cascade kicks in.
- **Secondary cascades exist.** Resolving one unresolved layer may pull TUs that introduce NEW unresolveds OR (worse) duplicate-symbol clashes with existing stubs. Each stub addition should be tested for the regression direction, not just the progress direction.
- **Source-relative `#include "..."` search is unfixable.** When the vendor TU does `#include "lua_socket/luasocket.h"` and the vendor header is at `language/lua/lua_socket/luasocket.h`, no `-I` path can shadow it. The shim-header-shadow doctrine has THIS limit. Workarounds : asm-rename bridge (failed due to secondary cascade) OR vendor patch.
- **At -98% cumulative, the remaining 2% requires a different tool.** Stub authoring has done its job ; the path to LINK GREEN is upstream/framework work, not more stubs.

### Why luasocket force_load didn't work — vendor-patch candidate

Investigation revealed pre-existing **upstream linkage-mismatch bug** :
- `vendor/.../language/lua/lua_socket/mime.h:21` : `extern int luaopen_mime_core( lua_State *L );` — NO `extern "C"`.
- `vendor/.../language/lua/lua_socket/luasocket.h:52` : same shape.
- The `.c` files are compiled with C linkage (since they're `.c`) — exports `_luaopen_socket_core` / `_luaopen_mime_core`.
- `aaalua_util.cpp` (C++ TU) includes those headers via `lua/lua.hpp` chain ; without `extern "C"`, the C++ compiler treats the decls as C++-linkage. It emits a reference to the C++-mangled name `_Z18luaopen_socket_coreP9lua_State` (or similar).
- Lib has only `_luaopen_socket_core` (C-mangled). C++ ref + C symbol = no match.

**Fix candidates** :
1. **Upstream patch** (one-line each, behavior-preserving on Win) : wrap the decls in `mime.h` and `luasocket.h` with `extern "C" { ... }`. Same family as the SystemUtils.h L181/184/187 candidate from c105.
2. **Tests-private shim** : shadow `mime.h` + `luasocket.h` in `tests/unit/aaalua_master_shim/lua_socket/` with `extern "C"` decls. No vendor edit.

Both are c112+ candidates. The current c111 stub doesn't address them — the 2 luasocket syms remain.

luasocket (2)          luaopen_socket_core / luaopen_mime_core (NEEDS extern "C" shim or vendor patch)
```

### New engineering insights

- **FINLINE-declared methods need `__attribute__((used, weak))` to emit out-of-line bodies on Mac.** AppleClang's `inline` keyword causes the compiler to skip emission when the stub TU has no call sites — even if other TUs need the symbol. `used` forces emission ; `weak` lets future real ports supersede. **First time this pattern was needed in the port.**
- **luasocket linkage-mismatch is the second pre-existing upstream bug surfaced by Mac cross-compile.** Pattern : every cross-platform port iteration reveals years-old guard / linkage misses that Windows tolerated silently. Document each as an upstream-patch candidate.
- **Predict-then-verify discipline holds approximately, with caveats.** c110 plan said 20 → 10 ; actual was 20 → 12. The 2-symbol miss was a structural surprise (luasocket linkage bug), not a stub-authoring miss. The remaining 10-bucket-by-symbol-count audit IS still trustworthy ; structural issues that need separate fix (vendor patches, shim shadows) are visible at link-attempt time, not at audit time.

### Engineering notes worth carrying forward

- **POSIX native = real port, not stub.** Per the NVIDIA->Metal substitution policy ("never stub when a real native port exists"), `system()` + `posix_spawn()` are real POSIX equivalents to `_popen` + `CreateProcessA` ; a noop stub would have been wrong.
- **Hermetic-lib doctrine.** A Mac sub-lib that calls only into `<spawn.h>` / `<sys/wait.h>` / `<cstdlib>` AND uses std::string instead of o_str carries zero engine-side dep weight. This is the cleanest pattern for porting tiny standalone subsystems while the bigger memcpy/CPU cascade is still blocked.
- **`/bin/true` does not exist on modern macOS.** Use `/usr/bin/true` / `/usr/bin/false` in test paths. (Discovered c104.)
- **err.h has single-include `#error` enforcement.** A direct `#include "err.h"` after pulling another header that already did `#ifndef AAA_ERR_H / #include "err.h" / #endif` fires "ERR_H included more than once." Always include via the ifndef-guarded idiom or via a single transitively-pulling header.
- **Refined c104+ sequencing for aaalua_master.cpp** (correcting c103's optimistic plan) :
  1. **c105** : aaalua_master.cpp partial port (header-parse smoke at minimum ; full link blocked on PARAM_DEF_* macros, c_lua_wrap, time_buf::TBUF_ADD, sysutils). Likely 2 sessions.

### Engineering notes worth carrying forward

- **Dead-function drop policy** : when a helper function exists in source but `main()` never calls it (and no other helper does either), drop it on Mac. ps_scanly's `vec3 sobel()` (the legacy 3x3 variant superseded by `sobel2()`) is the canonical example.
- **`1/x` strict promotion** : MSL `1 / float` is int division -> 0 if `float > 1`. Use `1.0 / float`. ps_scanly source had this latent bug ; Mac port fixes.

### Engineering notes worth carrying forward

- **`mod(x, y)` -> MSL `fmod(x, y)`.** GLSL `mod` uses floor (matches Euclidean modulo) ; MSL `fmod` uses trunc. Behaviour matches for positive operands (UV space). If a future shader needs negative operands' mod, switch to `x - y * floor(x/y)` explicitly.
- **Channel-swap quirks should be preserved verbatim with comments.** Engine GLSL has accumulated channel-mapping oddities (AndrejMetaImage red-to-.r, blue-to-.g, green-to-.b). Mac port preserves the literal mapping with `// engine source maps "X slider" to .Y multiplier (preserved)` so future audits don't "correct" it.
- **dotgrid / ink family share a tile-lookup-centre template.** Tile midpoint = `(floor(tex * tiles / max_uv) + 0.5) / tiles`. Then read base colour at midpoint, compute distance from midpoint, threshold-based mask. Pattern likely reusable across more shaders.
- **Catalog passed the 75-shader mark.** Compile-perf budget still under threshold ; no signs of test-runtime regression as the catalog grows. Plenty of headroom for c83+ batches.

| GLSL construct | Mac fix |

| `CONST int mode = aaa_fu_int[0];` at FILE SCOPE (line 4 outside any function) | MSL can't reference a uniform buffer at namespace scope -- move inside `fs_main` as a local : `int const mode = _aaa_ints.values[0];`. **New 5th substitution pattern : "file-scope uniform-dependent constant"**. |
| Tool emitted `return;` (void) inside the early-exit branch | MSL fragment must return float4 -- patched to `return col;`. **New 6th pattern : "tool's accumulator early-exit needs explicit return value"**. |

  6. **Tool early-exit `return;` inside fragment** (c75) → `return float4 expr;` (Metal requires the type).
- **First 3-texture shader in the catalog.** Demonstrates that the multi-binding shader pattern (tex0 + tex1 + tex2 + tex3 declared, only subset used) works cleanly through the MetalBackend pipeline.

### Engineering notes worth carrying forward

- **File-scope `uniform`-derived constants in GLSL must move inside the entry function in MSL.** GLSL allows `const T x = uniform_array[N];` at file scope ; MSL doesn't (uniform buffers aren't visible at namespace scope). Mechanical fix.
- **Tool's `_aaa_fragout` accumulator pattern doesn't handle early-exit `return;` in source GLSL.** When the original `void main()` uses `return;` to bail out, the tool currently emits the same `return;` -- but MSL's fragment signature is `fragment float4 fs_main(...)` which requires a float4 return. Each port needs the early-exit hand-patched to `return <value>;`. Adding this to the tool's transform pass would save a manual fix per shader.
- **The 6-pattern hand-patch playbook is now stable.** Future ports should expect at most 0-3 patches from this set ; truly novel patterns (new engine helpers, new vertex outputs) get added to the playbook session by session.

## Session 2026-05-26 (continuation 73) — tinyexr decode perf test (perf-labelled to 6)

**Agent:** Claude Opus 4.7 (autonomous, manual prompt fire)
**User:** Alex Mkwizu

### Purpose

Four consecutive Path A growth sessions (c69-72) built clean cadence. c73 pivots back to perf doctrine : closes the perf-coverage gap on the Phase 5 fifth beachhead (tinyexr, c67) which had only correctness tests, no throughput baseline. Mirrors the c54 stb_image perf shape for direct asset-pipeline comparison.

### What was done

**`tests/unit/tinyexr_perf_test.cpp`** -- 1 perf test : `TinyExrPerf.DecodeStaysUnderBudget`.

Approach :
- Encode once : 128x128 RGBA gradient (per-pixel + per-channel distinct floats so ZIP-compression has real entropy) via `SaveEXRToMemory( save_as_fp16=0 )` (FP32 = lossless).
- Sanity-check one decode succeeds before the loop.
- Warmup : 5 decodes (icache + ZIP inflate warmup), time discarded.
- Measured : 100 decodes wrapped in `os_signpost_interval_begin/end` named `"tinyexr.decode.loop"`.
- Budget : 50 ms per decode on M4 debug (EXR FP32 + ZIP overhead is meaningfully heavier than stb_image's PNG path).
- Stdout report includes Mpix/sec throughput headline for direct comparison with c54's stb_image baseline.

Result on M4 debug : **100 decodes of 128x128 FP32 RGBA EXR (7644 bytes compressed) in 354.20 ms** = avg 3.542 ms/decode = **4.63 Mpix/sec**. **14x headroom** under budget.

Comparison context :
| Library | Format | Bit depth | Mpix/sec |
|---|---|---|---|
| stb_image (c54) | PNG | 8-bit / channel | 52.7 |
| tinyexr (c73) | EXR FP32 | 32-bit / channel | 4.63 |

EXR is ~11× slower per pixel : FP32 reconstruction is 4× wider than PNG's 8-bit, plus tinyexr's `TINYEXR_USE_STB_ZLIB=1` zlib path is slower than stb_image's optimised inflate. Expected, well within budget.

**`tests/unit/CMakeLists.txt`** -- new `aaaseed_tinyexr_perf_tests` target. Links `aaaseed_tinyexr`. CTest label `perf;tinyexr`.

- Full ctest : **174/174 pass** (up from 173 = +1 TinyExrPerf), no regressions.
- Perf-labelled tests : **6** (was 5). Full vertical stack now : GPU frame, Lua dispatch, Path A compile (26 shaders), stb_image decode, .app end-to-end frame, **tinyexr decode**.

### Why this matters

- **Phase 5 5th beachhead now has perf coverage.** All 5 beachheads (stb_image, Lua 5.1, stb_truetype, LuaSocket, tinyexr) have either a perf test or a deterministic correctness test ; the asset-decode subset is now uniformly perf-measured (stb_image PNG + tinyexr EXR).

- **Perf coverage now spans 6 hot paths** : (1) GPU frame budget (gol_metal_perf), (2) Scripting interpreter dispatch (lua_bridge_perf), (3) Shader compile time (path_a_compile_perf), (4) PNG decode (stb_image_perf), (5) .app end-to-end frame budget (aaaseed_app_perf), (6) **EXR decode (tinyexr_perf)**. Compute bbox `[cursor-pad .. cursor+text_w+pad]` x `[8-pad/2 .. 8+line_advance+pad/2]` with 4px pad. Upload 6-vertex backdrop quad, draw with the solid shader. ### Engineering notes worth carrying forward

- **For single-header library vendors, prefer tagged releases over `master` / `release` branches.** Recent `release` branch heads frequently split a single-header into multiple files for development convenience -- breaking the "one curl, one header" vendor flow. Pin to a specific tag like `v1.0.10` known to be self-contained.
- **`TINYEXR_USE_STB_ZLIB=1` is a clean reuse pattern.** When two adjacent vendored libs need the same dep (here, deflate/zlib), share via the build-time flag rather than vendor twice. Saves disk space + symbol-collision risk.
- **EXR magic bytes 76 2F 31 01** are the format signature. The test asserts these so a future tinyexr upgrade that changes file format would surface immediately.
- **FP32 (32-bit float) EXR is lossless.** FP16 (half) is lossy at quantization boundaries. Tests that need bit-exact equality use `save_as_fp16=0`.

### Engineering notes worth carrying forward

- **Cascades can have 3+ layers.** Each "fix" surfaces the next layer. Survey upstream layers FIRST -- in this case, "what defines mem::b_cpy_use_*" would have shown memcpy.cpp owns them, which means lib + stub collision was inevitable.
- **When stub-symbol-name == lib-symbol-name, the linker can't pick one.** Static-lib semantics only skip .a's .o files when the symbol is ALREADY provided by an earlier .o. If a single .o (the stub) duplicates a symbol the lib's .o also defines, link FAILS rather than silently picks. Different from the o_str case which works because the stub-TU's .o provides those symbols first AND the lib's aaa_str.cpp .o stays unpulled.
- **Weak symbols are the escape hatch.** `__attribute__((weak)) bool mem::b_cpy_use_movsb = false;` lets the lib's strong def win without erroring on duplication. Use when collisions are unavoidable AND the lib's def has different semantics that should always win.
- **Honest deferral is engineering progress.** c66 = "we mapped a third layer". Each session's increment matters even if the cumulative goal isn't achieved.

### Engineering notes worth carrying forward

- **`namespace foo { ... }` in one TU + `class foo final { ... };` in another TU = ODR-permissible at link time but COMPILE-time poison.** Once any header in your TU declares `class foo`, references to `foo::bar` inside that TU lose the namespace path. The two stub files must never share a TU.

- **Engine authors often pre-bake null-safety into singletons.** `c_cpu::get_align_def()` has `if(one)` -- the author KNEW the singleton might be unavailable during static init. Always grep for that pattern in singleton accessors before deciding to stub vs port.

### Purpose

`aaalua_util.cpp` (884 LOC) is the foundation of the engine's Lua wrapper layer. c52 identified luasocket as the only remaining unported dep ; c55 cleared spy.h. This session vendors LuaSocket 3.1.0 from the engine tree, gets it linking on Mac, and proves `socket.core` + `mime.core` modules load. After this, `aaalua_util.cpp` has no further blockers.

### What was done

**New `cmake/aaa_luasocket.cmake`** : static lib `aaaseed_luasocket` from 14 .c files in `vendor/aaaseed-engine/Src/language/lua/lua_socket/` (12 portable + usocket.c for Mac sockets ; wsocket.c skipped, Unix-domain extras + serial skipped until a real consumer needs them).

**Build challenges resolved (in order)** :

1. **`FAR` macro undefined on Mac.** inet.c has `(const char FAR *)&yes` — `FAR` is a Win16 holdover that's empty on modern Windows but undefined on Mac. Fix : `target_compile_definitions( ... FAR= )`.

2. **`luaL_setfuncs` / `luaL_testudata` symbol resolution.** These are Lua 5.2+ / LuaJIT API names ; vanilla Lua 5.1.5 doesn't ship them. Engine's compat.h provides `#define luaL_setfuncs luasocket_setfuncs` redirects but gated on `LUA_VERSION_NUM==501`, and only 2 of 14 .c files include compat.h directly.

3. **Force-include order matters.** First attempt force-included compat.h directly — failed because compat.h uses `lua_State*` / `luaL_Reg*` types without including lua.h. Created `cmake/luasocket_mac_force_include.h` shim wrapper : sets `LUA_VERSION_NUM 501`, includes `lua.h` + `lauxlib.h`, then includes `compat.h`. CMake force-includes the shim instead.

4. **C vs C++ linkage ABI mismatch.** Initially compiled .c files as CXX (matching engine vcxproj convention). Vanilla Lua 5.1.5's `lua.h` declares the C API with bare `extern` -- no `extern "C"` wrap. Compiling luasocket as C++ produced C++-mangled `_Z8lua_pcallP9lua_StateiiI` calls against the C-linkage `_lua_pcall` symbol in libaaaseed_lua.a. Switched luasocket to plain C compile.

5. **luasocket.h's bare `extern "C"` block** then broke C compilation. Pre-approved one-line upstream patch : wrapped the block in `#ifdef __cplusplus` guards. Behaviour-preserving on Windows (still wraps when compiled as C++). 

**Test driver `tests/unit/luasocket_smoke_test.cpp`** -- 3 tests :
1. `LuaopenSocketCoreReturnsTable` -- calls `luaopen_socket_core`, asserts globals.socket is a table containing >= 4 of (gettime, select, tcp, udp, tcp4, udp4).
2. `LuaopenMimeCoreReturnsTable` -- calls `luaopen_mime_core`, asserts globals.mime is a table containing >= 4 of (b64, unb64, qp, unqp, qpwrp, wrp, eol, dot).
3. `SocketGettimeIsCallable` -- `socket.gettime()` returns positive double.

### Engineering notes worth carrying forward

- **When vendoring a C library that links against vanilla Lua, compile the library as plain C.** Vanilla Lua's `LUA_API extern` (no C++ wrap) means C++-mangled calls won't resolve. Even if a single header in the library has `extern "C" { ... }` blocks, gate those with `#ifdef __cplusplus` as a pre-approved cleanup and compile-as-C.
- **CMake's `-include foo.h` happens BEFORE every other include in the file.** If foo.h uses types from another header, foo.h itself must include that header. Don't expect the .c file's later includes to retroactively fix the force-included header.
- **Use a Mac-only shim header for force-includes**, not the engine's compat header directly. Keeps the engine vendor tree untouched (or minimally patched) AND gives the Mac build the include-order control it needs.
- **lib symbol mismatch debugging** : `nm libfoo.a | grep symbol_name` reveals mangled-vs-unmangled at a glance. The `__Z...` prefix is Itanium ABI C++ mangling ; matches `extern "C++"` or no-extern declarations. Use this to verify ABI before chasing CMake config bugs.

### Engineering notes worth carrying forward

Use `vector( N, T{...explicit fields...} )` to disambiguate. This bit once in continuation 61 ; pin the pattern for future POD-vector init.
- **MTKView display-link cadence drives the rolling FPS window naturally.** A 30-frame window at 60 Hz = 0.5 s of smoothing ; long enough that integer flicker on the FPS number is gone, short enough that real frame-rate changes appear within 0.5 s of happening.
- **Alpha-blend after the opaque catalog draw is the right order** for an overlay HUD. The catalog draw clears + writes opaque pixels ; the HUD's `(1, 1, 1, coverage)` output blends `src.a * src + (1 - src.a) * dst`, producing antialiased white text over whatever's underneath. No separate render target needed.
- **Per-frame string layout is cheap.** 18-character "FPS=XX.X frame=N" string at ~18 quads = 108 vertices = ~2 KB ; CPU side runs in microseconds.

2. Upload `atlas.alpha8` to an R8 MTLTexture via `MetalBackend::gen_texture_2d(..., R8) + texture_data_2d` (`bytes_per_row = atlas.width`).
3. Lay out "AB" at cursor (10, 30) → 12 vertices (2 quads × 6 verts) via c59 helper.
4. Create vertex buffer + uniform buffer (screen size `(128, 64)` in pixels).
5. Compile text MSL shader (vertex transforms pixel-space xy to NDC via uniform ; fragment samples R8 atlas, outputs `(1, 1, 1, coverage)`). Uses `ProgramDesc` with `Float2` position + `Float2` UV attributes, `BlendMode::AlphaBlend`.
6. Begin offscreen render pass on a 128x64 RGBA8 target with clear color (0.05, 0.05, 0.20, 1.0) → bright-blue-ish background so text pixels stand out.
7. `bind_program + bind_fragment_texture(atlas) + bind_vertex_buffer(verts, slot 0) + bind_vertex_buffer(screen_uniform, slot 1) + draw_arrays(Triangles, 0, 12)`.
8. End render pass, present.
9. Readback : for each glyph, walk its expected pixel bbox and count "bright" R-channel pixels (>150) ; sample one corner far from text and verify it's still the clear color.

**Assertions met** : `'A' bright pixels=18, max R=255 ; 'B' bright=23, max R=255 ; corner (R,G,B,A)=(13,13,51,255)` — the corner reading is the EXACT clear color (0.05 * 255 = 12.75 ≈ 13, 0.20 * 255 = 51). Text strokes saturate to full white (R=255) where coverage is 1.0.

**`tests/unit/CMakeLists.txt`** -- new `aaaseed_text_render_integration_tests` target. Links `aaaseed_text` + `aaaseed_gol_metal`. Passes `AAA_STB_TT_FONT_PATH`. CTest label `integration;text_render`.

The test's readback hits the expected pixel rows, proving the convention is consistent CPU→GPU.

### Engineering notes worth carrying forward

- **`bind_vertex_buffer(..., slot 1, 0)` is how you feed a vertex-shader constant buffer.** The Metal vertex stage reads `constant ScreenSize& screen [[buffer(1)]]`. The same slot works in the fragment stage via `bind_fragment_buffer` ; the bind helpers pick the right stage based on which one you call. Keep slot 0 for vertex data, slot 1+ for vertex-stage uniforms by convention.
- **Pixel-space → NDC math : `ndc.x = (px/W)*2 - 1`, `ndc.y = -((py/H)*2 - 1)`.** The negation on Y is critical for the engine's y-down screen-space ; without it, text would render mirrored along the horizontal axis. Pin this in the shader (already done in kTextMsl).
- **Bright-pixel counting is the right shape for "is text actually there ?" assertions.** Don't try to match pixel-exact patterns (varies with antialiasing + subpixel sampling) ; instead, count pixels that exceed a coverage threshold within the expected bbox. Loose enough to tolerate AA wobble, tight enough to catch a real "nothing rendered" regression.
- **Corner-readback for "clear color preserved" is the natural complement.** If the shader accidentally drew over the whole framebuffer, the corner check fails. Together with the in-bbox brightness check, the two assertions cover both false negatives (nothing rendered) and false positives (rendered too much).

## Session 2026-05-26 (continuation 59) — text quad layout helper (second .app HUD building block)

**Agent:** Claude Opus 4.7 (autonomous, manual prompt fire)

### Purpose

Continuation 58 landed the CPU-side glyph atlas. Continuation 59 lands the second building block : a pure-CPU "lay out a string as glyph quads" helper that produces a Metal-ready vertex buffer (x,y,u,v). With this in place, the GPU integration step for the .app HUD is reduced to : upload R8 atlas texture, compile a 30-line text MSL shader, draw the vertex buffer. Both the data (atlas) and the geometry (layout) are now testable in pure C++ -- the GPU work is the only thing that requires Metal context.

Pre-flight verification of MetalBackend : `GOL::TextureFormat::R8` already maps to `MTL::PixelFormatR8Unorm` (gol/gol_backend.h:48 + metal_backend.cpp:31), and `texture_data_2d` correctly accepts arbitrary `bytes_per_row`. No backend extension needed for single-channel atlas upload.

### What was done

**`src/text/glyph_atlas.h`** -- added :
- `struct Vertex2D { float x, y, u, v; }` -- 16 bytes per vertex, matches what the future text MSL shader will declare via vertex descriptor.
- `int layout_text_quads( atlas, text, cursor_x, cursor_y, out_vertices )` -- emits 6 vertices per printable glyph (two triangles forming a textured quad). Space (32) advances the cursor with NO geometry emitted. Bytes outside [32,126] (e.g. `\n`, `\t`, control chars) are silently skipped. Y-axis convention : grows downward (CoreGraphics / Cocoa top-left origin).

**`src/text/glyph_atlas.cpp`** -- implementation (~55 lines added) :
- Reads atlas's per-glyph `xoff`, `yoff`, `xadvance` plus the UV rect.
- Computes the quad's screen-space corners as `cursor + xoff/yoff` (top-left) and `(corner + uv_span * atlas_size)` (bottom-right) ; `quad_width = (u1 - u0) * atlas.width` since the packed atlas rect IS the glyph's pixel bbox.
- Pushes 6 `Vertex2D`s per quad in the canonical Metal CCW winding (looking from screen-space y-down).
- Returns quad count for callers that want to skip the `out_vertices.size() / 6` math.

**`tests/unit/glyph_atlas_test.cpp`** -- 4 new tests added (was 2, now 6 total) :
1. `LayoutTextQuadsAdvancesCursor` -- "AB" emits 2 quads / 12 vertices ; first quad starts at `cursor + A.xoff/yoff` with `A.u0/v0` UV ; second quad starts at `cursor.x + A.xadvance + B.xoff`.
2. `LayoutSpaceAdvancesWithoutGeometry` -- "A B" emits 2 quads (not 3) ; the B quad's x equals `A.xadvance + space.xadvance + B.xoff`.
3. `LayoutSkipsNonPrintableBytes` -- input `{'A', '\n', 'B'}` emits 2 quads ; the embedded newline is ignored.
4. `LayoutEmptyStringEmitsNoGeometry` -- empty string and null pointer both return 0 quads with no vertices.

### Engineering notes worth carrying forward

- **Six vertices per quad, NOT four indexed.** A glyph buffer with 1000 glyphs is 6000 vertices = 96 KB at 16 bytes/vert ; small enough that an indexed-draw with 4 vertices + 6 indices saves only ~24 KB. The non-indexed path is simpler (one draw_arrays call) and matches what the existing inline triangle in AAASeedMTKView already uses. Optimize later if a real MEU draws 100k glyphs.
- **Y-down convention applies engine-wide for screen-space.** Don't introduce per-subsystem y-axis conventions ; if a future text layer drew y-up, the HUD would need a math flip somewhere. Keep it y-down everywhere on Mac (matches Cocoa, MetalKit drawable size, NSScreen.frame). The OpenGL y-up flip is a vertex-shader concern, isolated to that one shader.
- **Skip non-printable bytes silently in the layout helper, do NOT advance.** A `\n` byte advancing by `space.xadvance` would surprise callers -- the C convention is that `\n` is "go to next line" not "advance by some pixels". Until a multi-line layout helper exists, skip-without-advance is the safe behaviour.

**Per-frame timing instrumentation in `AAASeedMTKView.mm`** :

- Bonus : invalidates the pump on `[NSApp terminate:]` to prevent stray timer fires.

- Asserts : `frames == 60`, `measured == 59`, `avg_ms < 16.0` (60 Hz budget), `max_ms < 50.0` (no stutter > 3x 60 Hz target).
- Stdout reports the parsed values + budgets for CI logs.

**`tests/unit/CMakeLists.txt`** -- new `aaaseed_app_perf_tests` target. CMake `add_dependencies` ensures `aaaseed_app` builds first. Passes `AAA_APP_BINARY_PATH` via `target_compile_definitions` using `$<TARGET_FILE:aaaseed_app>` generator-expression. CTest label `perf;app`.

## Session 2026-05-26 (continuation 47) — First Lua → engine integration proof

**Agent:** Claude Opus 4.7 (autonomous, ScheduleWakeup resume)
**User:** Alex Mkwizu

### Purpose

Lua is vendored (continuation 45). The engine is partially Mac-compiled. But until now, nothing has bridged the two : no Lua script has called engine code on Mac. This session closes that gap at the smallest possible scale -- wraps three engine math helpers (CLAMP / MIN / MAX from `code_utils/aaa_util.h`) as Lua-callable C functions, calls them from Lua scripts, verifies the semantics survive the roundtrip.

### What was done

**`tests/unit/lua_engine_bridge_test.cpp`** -- 5 integration tests that exercise the full Lua → C → engine → Lua roundtrip.

Pattern :
```cpp
int l_clamp( lua_State* L )
{
    double const a   = lua_tonumber( L, 1 );
    double const lo  = lua_tonumber( L, 2 );
    double const hi  = lua_tonumber( L, 3 );
    double const ret = CLAMP< double >( a, lo, hi );    // engine template
    lua_pushnumber( L, ret );
    return 1;
}
// then : lua_pushcfunction( L, l_clamp ) ; lua_setglobal( L, "clamp" )
// then : luaL_dostring( L, "return clamp( 5.0, 0.0, 10.0 )" )
```

5 tests :
1. `ClampWithinRangeReturnsInput` -- clamp(5, 0, 10) = 5
2. `ClampBelowLowerReturnsLower` -- clamp(-3, 0, 10) = 0
3. `ClampAboveUpperReturnsUpper` -- clamp(99, 0, 10) = 10
4. `MinAndMaxComposeInLua` -- max(min(7, 5), 3) = 5 (chains the engine bindings through Lua)
5. `ClampEquivalentToLuaSideExpression` -- sweep 9 sample values, cross-validate the engine binding against a pure-Lua reference clamp implementation. Catches behavioral drift.

CMake target `aaaseed_lua_engine_bridge_tests` links both `aaaseed_lua` (vendored Lua) and `aaaseed_code_utils` (engine code). `aaa_apply_engine_compile_flags()` provides the force-include for `aaa_util.h`. All 5 tests pass on M4.

### Why this matters

This is the **canonical pattern future `*_lua.cpp` ports will follow**. The engine has ~50 `*_lua.cpp` files (camera_lua, math_lua, img_lua, mat_lua, etc.) -- each wraps engine subsystem functions as Lua bindings via `AAALUACALL` macros. Those macros expand to roughly the same boilerplate as `l_clamp` above. By proving the pattern at the smallest scale, we de-risk the multi-session port of those wrapper files.

This also proves :
- Vendored Lua 5.1 + engine math helpers coexist cleanly.
- `aaa_util.h` is fully Mac-clean from a different consumer angle than the existing math_test.
- The `aaa_apply_engine_compile_flags()` macro works for test targets that mix Lua + engine headers.

### Cross-platform compat verification

Zero `vendor/aaaseed-*` touches. Test lives in `tests/unit/`. The Lua-binding pattern itself is identical to what the Windows engine uses (via `AAALUACALL` macros), so this code -- if generalized via the engine's macro layer -- would work on both platforms with no source diff.

### Engineering notes worth carrying forward

- **Cross-validation against a Lua-side reference** is the most robust shape for binding-correctness tests. The C binding and a hand-written Lua function compute the same answer over a sample sweep ; if they disagree, EITHER the binding has drifted OR the Lua reference has, both surfacing as a clear failure with the disagreeing value. Use this shape for future binding tests instead of hard-coded expected values.
- **`lua_Number` is `double` on Apple Silicon by default.** All numeric bindings should use `double` (lua_tonumber returns double, lua_pushnumber takes double). Don't introduce float-precision narrowing in the binding unless the engine function specifically requires float.
- **The 5-test bridge pattern is the right granularity.** Three "correctness" tests (within-range, below, above), one "composition" test (chains multiple bindings), one "cross-validation" test (sweep against reference). Future binding-file tests should follow this shape -- 5 tests per binding file gives reasonable coverage without bloat.

Continuation 44 landed stb_image — Phase 5's image beachhead. This session lands the OTHER major Phase 5 beachhead : Lua 5.1. Without Lua, no MEU runs (the engine is Lua-driven end-to-end). Vendoring Lua + a smoke test is high-leverage : unlocks the next layer of engine integration work (`*_lua.cpp` bindings, MEU script loading, etc.).

### What was done

**Vendored Lua 5.1.5 source** :
- Downloaded official release tarball from lua.org (`lua-5.1.5.tar.gz`, ~220 KB).
- Extracted `src/*` into `third_party/lua-5.1/` (30 .c files + 22 .h files + COPYRIGHT).
- Pinned to 5.1 per project doctrine -- engine's `*_lua.cpp` bindings assume the 5.1 C API surface ; bumping versions would break those bindings.

**Build wiring : `cmake/aaa_lua.cmake`** :
- Static library `aaaseed_lua` with 30 .c files. Explicitly enumerated (not glob) -- catches accidentally-vendored files outside the canonical set.
- `lua.c` (interactive CLI) and `luac.c` (bytecode compiler CLI) EXCLUDED -- those are application binaries, not library code.
- `LUA_USE_MACOSX` compile definition -- enables dlopen-based package.loadlib + the Apple-specific code paths in `loadlib.c` / `loslib.c`.
- Silenced AppleClang noise on upstream Lua code (`-Wno-deprecated-declarations`, etc.).
- Public include dir : consumers `#include "lua.h"` directly.
- Wired from root `CMakeLists.txt` via `include(aaa_lua)`.

**Smoke test : `tests/unit/lua_smoke_test.cpp`** -- 6 tests covering the C API surface engine bindings use most :

1. `OpenStateAndCloseClean` -- `luaL_newstate` + `luaL_openlibs` + `lua_close`. Round-trip without leaks (sanitizer-friendly).
2. `EvalArithmeticReturnsExpectedNumber` -- `luaL_dostring("return 6 * 7")`, read 42 off stack via `lua_tointeger`.
3. `StringLibStringFormat` -- exercises the standard `string` library (loaded via `luaL_openlibs`) ; verifies `string.format( '%d-%s', 7, 'aaa' )` returns "7-aaa".
4. `CFunctionRegisteredAndCalledFromLua` -- canonical engine-binding shape : `lua_pushcfunction(L, fn) ; lua_setglobal(L, "name")` ; then call from Lua, read result back. This is the entire AAALUACALL infrastructure boiled down.
5. `BadSyntaxReportsErrorWithoutCrashing` -- error path : invalid input must return non-zero AND leave a non-empty error string on the stack.
6. `LuaVersionMatches501` -- assert `LUA_VERSION_NUM == 501`. Pins the version against accidental upgrades.

All 6 pass on M4.

### Why this matters

**Lua is the engine's nervous system.** Every MEU is a Lua program (or loaded by one). Every UI choice in GaBuZoMeu runs through Lua. The bulk of engine flexibility is `c_obj_ui` objects exposed as Lua tables. Without Lua linked into the Mac build, ZERO real engine content can run.

This continuation closes that gap at the lib level. The engine's `*_lua.cpp` files (one per binding) can now link against `aaaseed_lua`. The next steps are :
- Port `language/lua/aaalua_*.h/cpp` -- the engine's Lua state wrapper. ~5-10 files.
- Port the `*_lua.cpp` binding files for each engine subsystem (math, image, draw, etc.). Big surface but mechanical -- each follows the same `AAALUACALL` pattern.

### Engineering notes worth carrying forward

`src/gol/gol_backend.h` :

- `begin_render_pass` : after binding slot 0 (existing path), iterate `additional_color_attachments[]` and bind slots 1-3 with matching load action + clear color.

Fixture :
- 16x16 source texture with distinct per-channel values (R=200, G=100, B=50).
- 4 distinct render targets bound to slots 0-3.
- Magenta clear color (255, 0, 255, 255) — discriminator : if MRT failed for any slot, it would stay magenta-cleared.
- Pipeline created via `create_program(ProgramDesc)` with `color_attachment_count = 4`.

Assertions verify the fragment shader's fan-out semantic on the M4 GPU :
- `rt0` ≈ (200, 100, 50, 255) — full RGB
- `rt1` ≈ (200, 0, 0, 255) — R channel only
- `rt2` ≈ (0, 100, 0, 255) — G channel only
- `rt3` ≈ (0, 0, 50, 255) — B channel only

Tolerances : 8 LSBs for matched channels (8-bit-to-float-to-8-bit roundtrip wobble), `< 8` for "should be zero" channels (catches magenta-clear-stayed bugs while permitting noise).

Test passes on the M4. **MRT confirmed end-to-end on Apple Silicon.**

### Why this matters

MRT is the first non-trivial backend feature added since the foundational Phase 3 work. The engine eventually needs MRT for :
- Deferred shading (G-buffer)
- Multi-target post-processing (ping-pong with two buffers in one pass)
- Picking + main color in one draw

## Session 2026-05-26 (continuation 40) — AppKit segfault root-cause fix : .app now renders a catalog shader

**Agent:** Claude Opus 4.7 (autonomous, ScheduleWakeup resume)
**User:** Alex Mkwizu

### Purpose

Continuation 39 surfaced an AppKit-context segfault on `gen_texture_2d` and hypothesized the root cause as a double-release of the `texture2DDescriptor` factory return. This session validates the hypothesis, applies the one-line fix, and re-enables the catalog draw path in the .app.

### What was done

**Audited metal-cpp ownership convention.**
- `MTL::TextureDescriptor::texture2DDescriptor(...)` is implemented as `Object::sendMessage<...>` with the ObjC selector `texture2DDescriptorWithPixelFormat_width_height_mipmapped_`.
- Per Apple's ObjC naming convention, any factory method NOT starting with `new`/`init`/`alloc`/`mutableCopy`/`copy` returns an **autoreleased** object.
- Confirmed in `third_party/metal-cpp/Metal/MTLTexture.hpp` -- the `_MTL_INLINE` definition uses `sendMessage`, which preserves Apple's ownership convention. Caller MUST NOT release.

**Fix applied : `src/gol/metal/metal_backend.cpp:309`.**
- Removed the `desc->release()` call after `MTL::TextureDescriptor::texture2DDescriptor(...)`.
- Replaced with a block comment explaining the convention and the continuation 39/40 root-cause story so the next agent doesn't reintroduce the bug.

**Audited all other `release()` call sites** in `metal_backend.cpp` (25 occurrences) :
- `*::alloc()->init()` patterns at lines 142 / 392 / 438 / 480 / 515 / 703 -- caller owns (+1 retain), MUST release. All paired correctly.
- All other releases are on objects retained explicitly via `retain()` -- correct.
- `texture2DDescriptor` was the ONLY factory-style call that was incorrectly released. One-shot fix.

**Re-enabled the catalog draw path in `AAASeedMTKView.mm`.**
- Restored the texture / uniform-buffer allocation that was bisected out in continuation 39.
- Restored the catalog-shader bind-and-draw in `drawInMTKView` ; triangle stays as fallback when bundle path fails.
- Restored the matching `delete_*` calls in `dealloc`.

**Verified end-to-end :**
- `aaaseed_app_smoke` integration test : **PASS** (was SEGFAULT).
- Full ctest : **117/117 pass**.
- Direct launch `aaaseed_app.app/Contents/MacOS/aaaseed_app --max-frames 3` exits cleanly + logs `catalog shader 'ps_Maa_add_scale' wired ; bundle path live.`
- The .app now renders the engine's `output = offset + src*scale` formula on the M4 GPU every frame, sampling a procedurally-generated 64x64 RGBA gradient with a small blue offset.

### Why this matters

After 10+ sessions of Path A catalog grinding, the .app bundle finally :
- Ships engine shader assets in its `Contents/Resources/`.
- Loads + compiles them from disk at runtime.
- Runs them through `MetalBackend::create_program_msl` -> binds textures + uniforms -> draws every frame on Apple Silicon GPU.

This is the **first time the catalog is doing real work** at the .app level, not just at the unit-test level. Phase 8 distribution is a real prospect now (the bundle has assets and renders them).

### Engineering note worth carrying forward

**metal-cpp ownership convention** : the rule is exactly Apple's ObjC rule.
- `alloc()->init()` -- caller OWNS the +1 retain. MUST `release()` when done.
- Factory class methods (named with anything other than `new`/`init`/`alloc`/`mutableCopy`/`copy`) -- return AUTORELEASED. MUST NOT `release()`. Calling `retain()` to keep alive past the next pool-drain is the explicit opt-in.
- The bug surfaces only when the autorelease pool drains at a different cadence than the unit-test harness expected. Standalone gtest's pool drains after `RUN_ALL_TESTS()` returns ; AppKit's drains per-event-loop-iteration. The latter catches the double-release sooner.

Audit any other `release()` in any other Mac code that follows a NON-`alloc()->init()` factory call. If a future MetalBackend feature uses (say) `MTL::RenderPipelineDescriptor::descriptor()` factory, the same rule applies.

### What was done

**Tool extension : non-prefixed uniform variants.**
- `analyse()` now detects bare `fu_float[]` / `fu_vec4[]` / `fu_int[]` (no `aaa_` prefix) and ORs the same `uses_aaa_fu_*` flags. Rationale : the Windows engine's `GLSL_shader.cpp` injection aliases prefixed and unprefixed forms to the same per-frame uniform array. The Mac port routes both through the same MSL struct + buffer-slot binding.
- Body substitution adds three regexes for the unprefixed forms : `\bfu_float[N]` → `_aaa_floats.values[N]`, similar for vec4 / int. Word-boundary anchor avoids accidentally matching already-translated `_aaa_floats` tokens.
- No new struct types ; no new buffer slots ; canonical names downstream. Cross-shader uniform layout stays single-sourced.

**Tool extension : singleton-texture handling in helper-mutation.**
- `_scan_helper_needs()` now returns a third list `singleton_texs` of `(name, slot)` pairs for non-array textures (e.g. `tex0`, `tex1`) referenced inside a helper body. Walks `info["tex_slots"]` for entries whose name doesn't contain `[`.
- `_mutate_helper()` adds a `texture2d< float > NAME` parameter to the helper signature for each singleton-tex it references.
- `_rewrite_call_sites()` passes the matching bare name through at each call.
- Old shaders that mix singleton textures (`uniform sampler2D tex0;`) with file-scope helpers using those textures now port cleanly — previously broken with `error: use of undeclared identifier 'tex0'` in helper bodies.

## Session 2026-05-26 (continuation 33) — Helper-mutation pass + tool maturity, catalog 6 → 11

**Agent:** Claude Opus 4.7 (autonomous, ScheduleWakeup resume)
**User:** Alex Mkwizu

### Purpose

Tool helper-mutation pass — the highest-leverage remaining Path A item per continuation 32's plan. The pass adds binding parameters to file-scope helper functions so they can access fs_main's textures / samplers / uniforms / varyings.

### What was done

**Tool maturity push** in `tools/glsl_to_msl/glsl_to_msl.py` :

1. **`strip_comments()`** pre-pass — removes C-style `/* */` and `//` comments BEFORE analysis. Eliminates the `ps_Maa_MixTwo` false-positive (had a commented-out `doit()` helper that the helper regex was seeing through comments). Preserves line numbers via newline-replacement so diagnostic reports stay aligned with the source.

2. **Helper-mutation pass** (~150 lines of Python). For each translated helper :
   - Scans body for binding references (`_aaa_tex_N` textures, `_aaa_samp`, `in.uv`, `_aaa_floats`, `_aaa_vec4s`, `_aaa_ints`).
   - Appends each detected binding to the helper's parameter list in canonical order.
   - Rewrites `in.uv` to `_aaa_uv` inside the helper body (the new local name).
   - Rewrites every call site in main (and other helpers) to pass the matching arguments. Uses regex with `[^()]*` arg matching — handles nested-paren-free call sites cleanly ; nested cases fall through to a clean Metal-compiler error rather than a wrong substitution.
   - Helpers that use NO bindings stay unchanged (zero-cost for helper-only-math files).

3. **Removed the helper TODO_PORT detection** in `analyse()` — the mutation pass handles it. Helpers no longer poison the "clean" classification.

4. **`aaa_fu_int[]` support** — symmetric with the existing `aaa_fu_float[]` / `aaa_fu_vec4[]` paths. New `AaaFuInts` struct, buffer-slot binding, body substitution. Surfaced by `ps_Maa_MixTwo`.

5. **`gl_FragColor` whole-word substitution** — was `gl_FragColor\s*=` → `_aaa_fragout =` (only matched bare assigns). Now `\bgl_FragColor\b` → `_aaa_fragout` (matches `gl_FragColor.xyz =`, `gl_FragColor.a +=`, etc.). Surfaced by `ps_Maa_MixTwo`.

6. **`texture()` (modern GLSL, no `2D` suffix)** — added the substitution. Engine shaders mix `texture2D` and `texture` ; both now resolve.

7. **`textureSize(t, lod)` substitution** — emits `int2(t.get_width(lod), t.get_height(lod))`. Surfaced by `ps_Maa_Blur_01` and `ps_Maa_edge_sobel`.

8. **Broadened `gl_TexCoord` substitution** — was `gl_TexCoord[N].SWIZZLE` → `in.uv` (swallowed the swizzle, broke single-component `.x`/`.y`). Now `gl_TexCoord[N]` → `in.uv` (swizzle rides through). Surfaced by `ps_Maa_Blur_01`.

**MSL prelude grew float4 overloads** of `gray()` and `compute_gray()`. Engine shaders call with both float3 and float4 args (texture samples). Surfaced by `ps_Maa_edge_sobel`.

### What was done

**`tests/unit/path_a_catalog_test.cpp` — Path A catalog test.**
- Iterates every file in `src/shaders/msl/*.metal`. For each, slurps the file, feeds source to `GOL::MetalBackend::create_program_msl`, fails if the Apple Metal compiler rejects the MSL. Uses `SCOPED_TRACE(filename)` so per-shader failures surface cleanly.
- Floor assertion : `ASSERT_GE(metal_files.size(), 5)` — catalog must never shrink silently. Future ports bump the floor.
- CMake : `target_compile_definitions(AAA_SHADERS_MSL_DIR="${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/src/shaders/msl")` so the test reads from the source tree without hardcoded paths. CTest label `regression;path_a`.

**Tool hardening (forced by the catalog test catching real bugs).**

Initial bulk run on 5 candidate shaders revealed three tool gaps. The catalog regression test caught them on the very first run — exactly its purpose. Hardenings landed :

1. **File-scope helper detection** : Added a regex in `analyse()` that catches `(return-type) name(args) {` at file scope (not `main`). MSL free functions can't access fs_main's `[[stage_in]]` / texture / sampler / buffer parameters, so helpers that touch those break compilation. The tool now emits TODO_PORT for each helper, downgrading "clean" to "needs review". Found ~25 shaders that previously claimed clean but actually had helpers.
2. **Engine-prelude function detection** : Added `gray()` and `compute_gray()` to TODO_PORT_PATTERNS. These are declared in the Windows engine's GLSL include-file prelude that GLSL_shader.cpp injects at register time ; without the Mac equivalent prelude, calls fail to link. Surfaced by `ps_Maa_threshold.frag` failing the catalog.
3. **`.s/.t/.p/.q` GLSL swizzles** : Added a substitution that rewrites `.stpq` cluster swizzles to `.xyzw`. MSL only accepts `.xyzw` and `.rgba`. Surfaced by `ps_Maa_move_pixel.frag` failing with `illegal vector component name 's'`.

Of the 25, ports landed and verified : `ps_Maa_4tex`, `ps_Maa_add_scale`, `ps_Maa_move_pixel`, `ps_edgeoverlay`, `ps_mrt_test`.

**Bugs discovered, NOT yet fixed (deferred to Group B follow-ups)** :
- Helper-function signature mutation (pass referenced bindings as helper params). Would unlock the 25-ish shaders the new helper-detection flags.
- Non-`aaa_`-prefixed uniform names (e.g. `fu_float[]` in `ps_slide.frag`). The tool only recognizes the `aaa_fu_*` family.

## Session 2026-05-26 (continuation 29) — glsl_to_msl mechanical tool, end-to-end verified

**Agent:** Claude Opus 4.7 (autonomous, ScheduleWakeup resume)
**User:** Alex Mkwizu

### Purpose

Path A scaling lever : with two hand-ported shaders already validated (continuations 25, 28), write the mechanical-substitution tool the strategy doc named as Group B's deliverable. Verify end-to-end : tool-generated MSL must compile via Apple's Metal compiler on the same `MTL::Device::newLibrary` path the engine uses.

### What was done

**`tools/glsl_to_msl/glsl_to_msl.py`** — ~430-line Python script implementing the GLSL → MSL transformations Continuation 25 + 28 did by hand. Doctrine intact : no SPIR-V, no Vulkan tooling. Pure regex + structural analysis. Three-mode behaviour :
- **Hard refuse (exit 2)** when source uses C++ preprocessor macro injection (`AAA_DEFINE_*`, `flight(`, `blend(`, `ST_AAA_BV`). These need Group C handling.
- **TODO_PORT (exit 1)** when source uses fixed-function GLSL (`gl_Vertex`, `gl_ModelViewMatrix`, `gl_NormalMatrix`, `gl_Color`, `ftransform`, `gl_Position`). Tool emits the line unchanged with a `// TODO_PORT:` marker above so a human finishes the port.
- **Clean port (exit 0)** when source uses only the supported vocabulary : texture sampling, gl_TexCoord, `aaa_fu_float[]` / `aaa_fu_vec4[]`, `gl_FragColor` / `gl_FragData`, basic types.

Substitutions covered (extensible) :
- `vec2/3/4` → `float2/3/4`, `mat2/3/4` → `float2x2/3x3/4x4`, ints + uints similar.
- `texture2D(t, uv)` → `t.sample(_aaa_samp, uv)`.
- Sampler-array `aaa_tex2d[N]` flattened to one `texture2d<float>` per slot, named `_aaa_tex_N`.
- `gl_TexCoord[0].{xy,st,xyz,...}` → `in.uv` (collapsed to the 2D varying we pass from vs_main).
- `aaa_fu_float[N]` / `aaa_fu_vec4[N]` → explicit `constant AaaFuFloats& _aaa_floats` / `AaaFuVec4s& _aaa_vec4s` at buffer slot 0/1, with `.values[N]` indexing.
- `gl_FragColor = X` → `return X` from fragment ; `gl_FragData[N] = X` → MRT struct with `[[color(N)]]` attachments.
- `dFdx`/`dFdy` → `dfdx`/`dfdy` ; `mod` → `fmod`.
- File-scope helper functions (e.g. `float getGray(vec4)`) preserved and translated alongside the body.
- Emitted prelude includes `#include <metal_stdlib>`, `using namespace metal;`, `VertexOut`, oversized-full-screen-triangle `vs_main`, the right struct decls for detected uniforms.

**Validation : tool-generated MSL feeds the Metal compiler cleanly.**
- Ran the tool on `ps_Maa_4tex.frag` (3rd engine shader). Output went straight into `tests/unit/shader_msl_port_test.cpp` as `ShaderMslPort.PsMaa4tex_ToolGeneratedMslBuildsProgram`. Test goes through `GOL::MetalBackend::create_program_msl` — same engine front door real production code uses. **Test passes.** Apple's Metal compiler accepts the tool's output as-is.
- Also re-ran the tool on `ps_Maa_add_scale.frag` (which we hand-ported in continuation 28). Tool produced semantically equivalent MSL (different layout from the hand-port but same logic) — confirms the tool generalises.

**Path A shader #3 landed via the tool : `src/shaders/msl/ps_Maa_4tex.metal`**.

### Engineering notes worth remembering

- **`AAA_OS_MAC()` vs `__APPLE__`** : the engine's `AAA_OS_MAC()` macro requires `aaa_type.h` to have been included first. For early-in-header gates (before the force-include + any project header), use `#if defined(__APPLE__)` directly. This is the second time this distinction has mattered (first was the aaa_mem.cpp partial-port macro fix in continuation 25). Doctrine update for agent_profile.md / philosophy.md if it bites a third time.
- **Mach-O static-lib weak symbols** : when a .cpp lives in a static lib AND a duplicate definition lives in a .o linked into the executable, the linker silently picks the .o's strong symbol. We rely on this to keep test execs hermetic from `err_print` / `VERBOSE_PRINT_STRING` deps while still shipping the real aaa_mem.cpp in `aaaseed_app`. Documented in todo.md.
- **GPU debug-marker pop balance** : Metal will assert (or worse, silently corrupt) if you call `popDebugGroup` on an encoder that never `push`ed. The `_debug_label_was_pushed` flag handles the `debug_label == nullptr` case correctly ; the new render test guards this corner.

### Bugs found and fixed (real-world post-agent integration)

These surfaced when actually compiling the agent's work into `aaaseed_code_utils` :

1. **Wrong macro name (AAA_OS_DARWIN)** — agent followed my hallucinated brief instead of grepping aaa_type.h. Even though I told agents to verify, one used the wrong name. Fixed via sed in aaa_mem.cpp + corrected briefings for the 4 new agents. **Lesson : agents WILL trust the prompt's claims about source-code symbols ; the prompt itself must be ground-truthed against actual code.**

2. **`#define _stat64 stat` macro alias is broken** — the agent's clever-but-wrong alias caused name resolution to confuse `struct stat` (TYPE) with `stat()` (FUNCTION) at use sites. Replaced with `typedef` + inline wrapper functions :
   ```cpp
   #if AAA_OS_WINDOWS()
   typedef struct _stat64 aaa_stat_t;
   inline INT32 aaa_stat ( C_PCHAR_C path, aaa_stat_t* buf ) { return _stat64 ( path, buf ); }
   #elif AAA_OS_MAC()
   using aaa_stat_t = struct stat;
   inline INT32 aaa_stat ( C_PCHAR_C path, aaa_stat_t* buf ) { return ::stat ( path, buf ); }
   #endif
   ```
   Same pattern applied to `_mkdir` / `_chdir` / `_getcwd` in `aaa_dir.cpp` — function-style macros there were also miscompiling.

3. **`<fcntl.h>` defines `FREAD` / `FWRITE` macros** — Apple's `<sys/fcntl.h>` (pulled in by `<fcntl.h>`) `#define`s `FREAD 0x1` and `FWRITE 0x2`, which token-replace the engine's `c_file::FREAD` / `c_file::FWRITE` method names. Fixed with explicit `#undef FREAD / #undef FWRITE` after the system header includes.

4. **`unsigned char(0xFF)` non-conforming C++** — pre-existing engine code in `aaa_file.cpp` (BOM declarations) using functional-cast on multi-token type. AppleClang strict, MSVC lenient. Fixed via `static_cast<unsigned char>(0xFF)` (pre-approved upstream patch).

5. **`std::chrono::clock_cast` not in libc++ on AppleClang 21** — C++20 feature missing for `file_clock`. Hand-rolled duration-based conversion (file_clock and system_clock share Unix epoch on Darwin) gated to `#elif AAA_OS_MAC()`.

6. **Force-include of `aaa_build_config.h` does NOT pull in `aaa_type.h`** — so `AAA_OS_WINDOWS()`/`AAA_OS_MAC()` macros are undefined at file top. Added explicit `#include "aaa_type.h"` before the platform-gate. (Engine relies on the first project header to drag it in transitively ; agent put platform gate BEFORE any include.)

7. **`C_PCHAR_C p = path; ++p` won't compile** — `C_PCHAR_C` is `const char* const` (double-const). Agent used the project type macro thinking it's "const-pointer to const char" (single const). Replaced with plain `char const*` for the loop cursor in `aaa_file.cpp`.

8. **`net` symbol mangling** — agent stub provided `c_net_stub _net;` (C++ source name `_net`, mangles to `__net`) but engine references `net` (C++ source, mangles to `_net`). Fixed stub : `class c_net; c_net* net = nullptr;` — `net` mangles to `_net` matching engine references. The runtime path guarded `if( net && ...)` so the null pointer is safe.

9. **Heavy transitive deps for err.cpp** — agent's port is correct but `err.cpp` includes `infrastructure/layer/layer.h`, `ui/aaa_menu.h`, `ui/dialog_dev.h` — none Mac-ported yet. Deferred err.cpp integration ; stubbed `PRINT_STRING` + `debug_break_if` in `test_engine_stubs.cpp` for the log test to link.

- Pure Apple Metal — no SPIR-V, no Vulkan IR. Path A's GLSL → MSL is direct (`MTL::Device::newLibrary(NS::String*, ...)`). No `xcrun metal` toolchain dependency at build time either (runtime MSL compile path).
- Multi-agent parallelism is GENUINELY effective for independent file-level ports, but the integration phase needs main-context attention. The agents in this session each produced reasonable ports but ALL hit non-trivial issues at integration time. Allocate roughly equal time to (a) parallel agent work and (b) sequential integration after.
